items.prompt: Black to move. Tap the black pawn that two white pieces attack.

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack f7.
Only one white piece attacks e5.
Only one white piece attacks h7.

hints: Look at the white queen and the white bishop. Which black pawns sit on their lines?
Three black pawns are attacked. Count the attackers of each.
The queen and the bishop both look at the same square on Black's second row, next to the king.
items.explain: The white queen attacks the pawns on e5, f7 and h7. The bishop on c4 also attacks f7, so f7 is the pawn attacked twice, and only the king defends it. That is where a threat will appear.

items.prompt: Black to move. If Black did nothing useful and White moved next, what would White play to win material or checkmate? Name that move, or choose 'No threat'.

claims.statement: If Black passes, the pawn takes the knight and White comes out ahead.
The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6.
No black piece is loose: the knight is defended.

hints: Which white piece just moved, and what does it attack now?
The knight has a defender. Does that make it safe from a pawn?
The pawn on e5 can capture on f6.
items.explain: The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6. The g7 pawn defends the knight, so it is not loose, but a pawn is worth less than a knight. After pawn takes knight and the recapture, White is ahead.

feedback_by_move.d2d4: That is not a capture or a check. The real threat is the pawn on e5 taking the knight.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the knight on f6 can move to where no white piece attacks it right now.

claims.statement: The knight has exactly these five squares.
No white piece attacks d5.
No white piece attacks e4.
No white piece attacks g8.
The white queen attacks g4.
The white queen attacks h5.

hints: First list the five squares the knight can reach.
For each, ask which white piece could capture there next.
The queen on d1 looks along a long diagonal. Which two of the knight's squares are on it?
items.explain: The knight can reach five squares. The white queen sees g4 and h5 along the diagonal that the pawn move opened, so those two are not safe. Nothing attacks d5, e4 or g8. Safe is not the same as good: it only means the knight cannot be taken at once.

feedback_by_move.f6g4: The queen on d1 attacks g4 along the open diagonal, so the knight would be lost.
feedback_by_move.f6h5: The queen attacks h5 along the same diagonal.

items.prompt: White to move. If White did nothing useful and Black moved next, what would Black play to win material or checkmate? Name that move, or choose 'No threat'.

claims.statement: If White passes, the pawn takes the bishop and Black wins material.
The bishop on a4 is the only loose white piece.

hints: Black's last move was a pawn move. What does that pawn attack now?
Is the piece it attacks defended?
The pawn on b5 attacks the bishop on a4, and nothing defends the bishop.
items.explain: The pawn on b5 attacks the white bishop on a4. Nothing defends that bishop, so it is loose, and a pawn costs less than a bishop. If White ignores it, the pawn captures the bishop.

items.prompt: White to move. Make Black's threat fail without losing material.

claims.statement: Retreating to b3 keeps the bishop safe and is among the engine's best moves.
Taking the pawn loses the bishop.

hints: The bishop is attacked by a pawn. Which squares on its diagonal are safe?
One retreat keeps the bishop aiming at the black king's side. Which?
Along the diagonal toward Black's kingside, the bishop goes to the third row.
items.explain: From b3 the bishop is out of the pawn's reach and still looks at f7. Moving a threatened piece to a square nothing attacks is the simplest answer to a threat.

feedback_by_move.a4b5: The pawn on a6 takes the bishop on b5. You lose the bishop for a pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's last move was the rook to e1. Which of your pieces is loose (attacked, and not defended)? Kings do not count.

claims.statement: The knight on e4 is the only loose black piece.

hints: List the black pieces that a white piece attacks.
Check the knights and the pawn in the middle one by one for a defender.
The rook on e1 now looks up the open file at e4.
items.explain: The rook on e1 attacks the knight on e4 along the open e-file, and no black piece defends that knight. The pawn on e5 and the knight on c6 are attacked too, but each has a defender.

items.prompt: Black to move. Choose a safe move that leaves nothing attacked.

claims.statement: These moves are all close to the engine's best.
The knight move to b4 loses a piece.
Retreating the c6 knight to b8 loses the e5 pawn and more.

hints: Before you move, ask what each move leaves attacked.
The knight on c6 does a job. Which pawn would lose its defender if it left?
A pawn move or the bishop to e7 keeps everything protected.
items.explain: Moves such as d5 or Be7 develop or support the position and leave nothing attacked and undefended. The knight on c6 defends the e5 pawn, so moving it away loses that pawn, and b4 is attacked by the a3 pawn.

feedback_by_move.c6b4: The a3 pawn attacks b4. The knight would be lost for a pawn.
feedback_by_move.c6b8: The knight was the only defender of the e5 pawn. The white knight takes it.
feedback_by_move.c6a5: The knight was the only defender of the e5 pawn. The white knight takes it.
feedback_by_move.f8b4: The a3 pawn attacks b4, so the bishop would be lost.
feedback_by_move.f6h5: The queen on d1 attacks h5 along the open diagonal.

items.prompt: Black is thinking of playing the bishop to b4, hoping to pin the knight. White would reply. Does this move lose material for Black?

claims.statement: The a3 pawn attacks b4.
The move loses a piece for a pawn at most.

hints: Where would the bishop land? Which white piece attacks that square?
What is a pawn worth next to a bishop?
The pawn on a3 attacks b4.
items.explain: The bishop lands on b4, a square the white pawn on a3 attacks. Black could win a pawn back at most, but the bishop is worth more. This is the first leak: the moved piece lands on an attacked square.

items.prompt: Black to move. If Black did nothing useful and White moved next, what would White play to win material or checkmate? Name that move, or choose 'No threat'.

claims.statement: If Black passes, the queen takes on f7 and it is checkmate.

hints: Which two white pieces aim at the same square?
That square is next to Black's king. Who defends it?
The queen can capture on f7 and the bishop protects the queen.
items.explain: The queen and the bishop both aim at f7, and only the king defends it. The king cannot capture the queen because the bishop protects her. So the queen taking on f7 would be checkmate.
